idiom_name: hand-written recording struct behind a function-pointer seam
implementation_notes: C offers no runtime interception, so the collaborator must be reached through a function pointer (or a link-time seam such as a weak symbol) and the test installs a recorder: a struct holding the call log (count, captured arguments, order) plus forwarder functions that append to the log and then delegate to the real implementation. What replaces the classic spy object is this recorder struct plus a set of spy functions registered at the seam; CMock generates the same shape from headers (expectations plus callbacks for recording), but its model is expectation-first, so hand-rolled recorders remain the direct realization.
pitfalls: The recorder is global mutable state: a shared log races under threads and leaks between tests - pass a per-test context struct through the function pointer, or reset it in setUp.

Capturing string arguments requires copying; storing the caller's char* leaves the log pointing at freed or reused buffers (snprintf into a fixed field is the cheap fix, with its own truncation caveat).
Forwarding means the real implementation runs: real I/O still happens, so replace the forwarder when the test must stay hermetic.
